text:
Barrett Hayton has turned into one of the quietly effective players on a Utah team that controls a lot of games. With him on the ice at five on five, the Mammoth have taken 64% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), more than ten points better than when he sits. Since Kailer Yamamoto went out, he's been centring Clayton Keller and Anders Lee.

The points, 10 in 18, are about what that role should produce, but they've come almost entirely as assists. He's shooting 5.7% against a normal range of about 9 to 13%, and his 3.79 expected goals say he's nearly two goals short. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he gets on the end of the best passes, across the slot and from behind the net, which are the shots that go in most often. Evolving-Hockey's view of last season was more modest (0.3 wins above replacement, mostly from defence). The fifth overall pick from 2018 has never quite become a star. This might be the season he becomes something useful instead, which is underrated.
